quotes.text: Every meal is a small decision about the kind of day you want to have.
Your body is the only vehicle you get for the whole journey, and it runs on what you put in it.
Food is not the enemy and it is not a prize. It is the fuel behind everything else you love doing.
The energy you spend on your dreams was chopped, cooked or picked at some point today.
Strong days begin on the plate, long before they begin on the calendar.
Your heart beats roughly a hundred thousand times a day, and it runs on what you eat.
A meal is a deposit into how you will feel at four in the afternoon.
A good meal is quiet proof that you take your own life seriously.
Your body rebuilds itself from what you eat. In a real sense, tomorrow’s you is being made today.
You will spend your whole life in this body. What you feed it is the most personal decision you make three times a day.
Long before there were energy drinks, there was a proper breakfast, and it still works.
Energy is not something you find. It is something you eat, drink, sleep and walk your way into.
Feeling flat at three o’clock is often just your body asking what happened to lunch.
A well-fed body does not shout. It quietly lets you get on with your life.
Good food will not make everything easy, but it makes a great many things possible.
The plate in front of you is the smallest place where you can make a big difference.
To a body that rebuilds itself every day, no meal is small.
Imagine caring for your body like something you plan to keep for ninety years. Because you do.
Your brain is about two percent of your weight and uses roughly a fifth of your energy. Feed it on purpose.
Trillions of microbes live in your gut, and they eat what you eat. You are never dining alone.
More than half of you is water. A glass of it is the simplest kindness you can offer your body.
Hunger is information, not an emergency. Meet it with something that will carry you through the afternoon.
A body with enough of the right things is calmer, steadier and easier to live in.
The strength to lift, run, focus and forgive is partly assembled in the kitchen.
Nobody has ever regretted a good breakfast on a hard morning.
Think of food as the quiet team behind everything your body does well.
A single well-chosen meal will not change your life. A life of them will.
Fuel is not the same as filler. Your body knows the difference by evening.
It is hard to be your best when you have been running on fumes since morning.
Your energy tomorrow is being decided by the next thing you put on your plate.
Every colour on the plate is a different tool your body knows how to use.
What you eat becomes the muscle you move with, the skin you wear and the mood you carry.
The kitchen is where energy gets made, long before it gets spent.
Regular meals of real food are a promise to your body that you will not forget it.
A day begins long before your alarm. It begins with what you decided to eat last night and this morning.
Your body has been working for you since before you were born. Feeding it well is a fair way to say thanks.
When the body is well fed, the mind stops negotiating with hunger and gets back to work.
A rested, well-fed body is the most underrated productivity tool ever invented.
Between the alarm and the evening, you are mostly running on what you ate.
Real energy tends to arrive slowly and stay for a long time.
When you fuel your body properly, you lend it to everything you care about.
Nothing you want to achieve gets easier on an empty or careless stomach.
Your body never gets a day off from being your body. Give it something worth working with.
The best investment you will ever manage is the one on your plate.
A balanced plate is a small, daily vote for the person you are becoming.
Every plate is a quiet argument between what is easy now and what is good later. Both deserve a hearing.
The freshest thing you can do for your energy is a glass of water and a handful of something real.
You do not have to earn your food. You only have to choose it well and enjoy it.
Think of your body as the house you live in. Food keeps the lights on and the walls strong.
Kindness to your body begins the moment you decide what goes on the plate.
An ordinary Tuesday meal, chosen well, does more for you than a perfect plan you never start.
Food gives you the day. What you do with it is up to you.
Rest is half of energy and food is the other half. Neither deserves to be an afterthought.
A little planning in the morning saves a lot of guessing at night.
Good fuel does not make you perfect. It makes you steadier, and steadier is what matters.
The body keeps no secrets about how it was fed. It shows up in every step and every mood.
Give your body a reason to say yes to the day.
The stairs feel shorter on days you have eaten well.
Nobody sees the breakfast that powered a great afternoon, but everybody feels it.
Some days the bravest thing you can do is eat a proper meal and get on with it.
A body that has been looked after tends to look after you back.
Eating well does not add hours to the day. It makes the hours you have feel bigger.
